Done. The LoRA merge is complete and verified.

**What was built:** `out/T5/plan.yaml` loads the base and adapter under two aliases, computes each layer's `B @ A` with a single capture-based `matmul` into a temporary delta, scales the deltas by 2, upcasts the 16 base weights to float32, adds the deltas in place, casts back to float16, deletes the deltas, and asserts the required checks before writing. Output is sharded at 512 MiB into `out/T5/`.

**Executions:** 2. The first failed because I wrote the matmul `from_b` reference with regex-escaped dots. In ternary transforms only `from_a` is a regex, while `from_b` and `to` are rewrite templates of its captures, so the backslashes were kept literally and no adapter A tensor matched. The second run passed all assertions and wrote the checkpoint.

**Verification, read-only, outside the plan:**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Tensor count / key set | 244, identical to base |
| Shapes and dtypes | all match base |
| Unchanged tensors bit-exact | 228 of 228 |
| Merged weights vs. fp16(W + 2·B@A) in fp32 | relative Frobenius error 0 |
| Shards | 4 files, each under 536,870,912 bytes, index maps every tensor |

The self-report is at `out/T5/REPORT.md`, listing the one failed execution, the `from_b` template pitfall, and two documentation gaps: the ternary rewrite semantics are not explicit, and mixed-dtype behavior of `add_` is undocumented.
